newsitem.title: USA: Parker FX Index up 2.81 pct in 1996 -- report.
newsitem.headline: Parker FX Index up 2.81 pct in 1996 -- report.

text.p: Parker Global Strategies reported on Monday that its Parker FX Index was up 2.81 percent in 1996 with 58 of the 61 programs in the Index reporting.
Virginia Parker, president of Parker Global, noted that 1996 proved a strong year overall for currency managers.

"Much of the gains were achieved during the fourth quarter as the dollar continued to surge against the Japanese yen, the deutschemark and other European currencies," said Parker, who created the Index.
The Parker FX Index is a performance-based benchmark that measures risk adjusted returns of global currency managers.
The median return for the Index was up 2.41 percent in 1996, Parker Global said. Results for 1996 were positive for 39 of the 61 programs reporting.
Cyber Capital L.L.C of New York City was top risk adjusted performer for 1996, with a risk adjusted gain of 18.60 percent and a reported gain of 32.92 percent, it said.
SBC Warburg of London achieved the second best performance, with a risk adjusted gain of 11.87 percent and a 22.30 percent rise on a reported basis.
Goldman Sachs Asset Management of London, which was up 11.67 percent on a risk adjusted basis and 11.25 percent on a reported basis, ranked third for the year, Parker Global said.
